newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares close higher but outlook skittish.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares close higher but outlook skittish.

text.p: Dutch shares started rising at the open and closed substantionally higher on Monday as a stronger dollar and a recovery in the bond market supported most shares.
"The overall sentiment was positive," said one dealer, adding the rise seemed to be overdone.
"The Dutch AEX index closed 2.7 percent higher, while other markets showed less substantial gains," he said.
The AEX index closed 19.16 points higher at 727.59.
The AMX index for medium-sized companies gained 3.4 percent, or 37.23 points to 1131.62.
Semiconductor equipment maker ASM Lithography and software maker Baan were among the stocks which outperformed the mid-cap index.
Dealers said high tech stocks were in demand since the sector had performed well in the United States last Friday.
"High tech stocks were catching up here," said one dealer, adding the reaction was a bit overdone.

ASM Lithography jumped 27.00 guilders or 20 percent to 162.00 guilders. Last week, ASM Lithography lost 7.4 percent. But dealers said they could not figure out why ASM Litho rose so strongly. "It seems there is no story behind it," said one.
Baan gained 3.70 guilders at 89.50, after touching a day's high of 92.50 guilders earlier.
Dealers said that high tech stocks and financials were likely to be the most volatile sectors in the days ahead as both segments had performed very well today.
"The whole market is expected to fluctuate as investors remain nervous," said one dealer.
Bank-insurer ING rose 2.80 guilders to 73.40 guilders and Fortis Amev jumped almost 4.5 percent or 3.00 guilders to 70.50.
Insurer Stad Rotterdam rose another 3.00 guilders to 81.00.
Last Friday the medium sized insurer announced it was planning to buy the remaining 45 percent of smaller fellow-company De Amersfoortse.
Stad Rotterdam is expected to announce 1996 profits of some 155 million guilders on Thursday versus 133 million in 1995.

Electronics firm Philips rose 4.20 guilders to 87.70 on last week's news that it was planning to sell nine small subsidaries. Publisher Wolters Kluwer closed 3.70 guilders higher at 231.50 after it announced it was not planning a share split in the short term.

Dealers said Wolters Kluwer was seen as a good buy. "Not because of today's announcement, but the stock has been underperfoming the market and to me it seems a better buy than Elsevier," said one dealer.
